scope: All physically changed/new native trace geometries and new/relocated native barrel positions relative to Source23. No full connectivity graph or broad full-board clearance duplicate.
methods: Stable geometric/native ownership signatures identify scope despite source/native ID renumbering.
Authenticated native source ownership selects exemptions; every foreign pad, trace, all-layer PTH/barrel and actual regenerated BREP pour remains a possible obstacle.
0.501 mm broad-phase copper sweep bounds every trace clearance rule tested; exact center-geometry plus stroke-radius distance is used in narrow phase.
Trace/PTH/pour/via foreign trace gaps are .20 mm; NPTH trace gap .50 mm. Proposed relocated through barrels screen all four copper layers plus drill spacing, SMT via-in-pad and board edge.
Foreign via-to-via copper .15 mm is declared policy; below .20 mm preferred spacing is reported separately. Numerical clearance acceptance tolerance 1e-7 mm.
limitations: Scope does not establish whole-board physical continuity, final ground contact quality, current capacity or converter stability.
Ideal geometry does not establish manufacturing tolerances or bench behavior.
Other team roles own full-board connectivity, whole-board shorts, ground/reference and parts/source/Gerber gates.
